announcements.text: Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control, Orlando, Florida, has been awarded an $825,975,480 modification (P00020) to previously awarded (FA8682-24-C-B001) for the Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile and Long Range Anti-Ship Missile Large Lot procurement. This modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $10,480,052,550 from $9,654,077,070. Work will be performed in Orlando, Florida, and is expected to be completed July 31, 2030. Fiscal 2024 missile procurement funds in the amount of $2,150,000; fiscal 2024 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,453,033; fiscal 2025 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $219,510,682; fiscal 2025 missile procurement funds in the amount of $378,735; fiscal 2026 missile procurement funds in the amount of $72,767,776; fiscal 2026 weapons procurement funds (Navy) in the amount of $49,219,714; fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $4,159,804; fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $686,013; and Foreign Military Sales funds in the amount of $11,070,988, are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: CAE USA Inc., Tampa, Florida, has been awarded a $45,319,364 firm-fixed-price contract for a full flight simulator and logistics support package. This contract provides for the acquisition and installation of one Federal Aviation Administration, Level D qualified 747-8i full flight simulator at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, and the acquisition of an initial logistics support package. Work will be performed in Tampa, Florida; Saint-Laurent, Quebec, Canada; and Joint Base Andrews, Maryland; and is expected to be completed by March 30, 2029. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2025 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $43,628,111 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Lifecycle Management Center, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity (FA8641-26-C-B002).

announcements.text: Lockheed Martin Corp., Liverpool, New York, was awarded a $257,278,109 firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, and cost-only modification to a previously awarded contract (N00024-23-C-6411) to exercise options for production, spares, production support material, engineering support, and hardware repair of components for MK 48 Heavyweight Torpedo All Up Round in support of the MK 48 MOD 7 Heavyweight Torpedo program. This contract combines purchases for the Navy, the Royal Australian Navy, and the Foreign Military Sales program. Work will be performed in Liverpool, New York (57%); Clearwater, Florida (37%); and Braintree, Massachusetts (6%), and is expected to be completed by September 2029. Fiscal 2025 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $150,647,159 (62%); fiscal 2026 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of (7%); fiscal 2024 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,216,670 (1%); and funding from foreign partners in the amount of $74,799,495 (30%), will be obligated at the time of award. Funding in the amount of $1,216,670 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. (Awarded Sept. 3, 2026).

announcements.text: Moog Military Aircraft LLC, Elma, New York, is being awarded $16,547,505 firm-fixed-price contract for the overhaul of the swashplate actuator (7RH 1680-014749949) supporting V-22 sustainment. Work will be performed in East Aurora, New York; and Fleet Readiness Center East (FRC-E), Havelock, North Carolina, as part of a public-private partnership between Moog and FRC-E. Work is expected to be completed by March 2029. Fiscal 2026 working capital funds in the amount of $16,547,505 will be committed at the time of award and those funds will not expire. One source was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (c)(1) and one offer was received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon System Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania is the contracting activity (N00383-26-C-BA21).

announcements.text: Huntington Ingalls Inc., Pascagoula, Mississippi, is awarded a $13,217,537 cost-plus-award-fee contract for Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) Planning Yard support for advanced planning, class engineering, and primary support of the modernization of the LCS Class. This contract includes options which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this contract to $742,848,205. Work will be performed in Pascagoula, Mississippi, and is expected to be completed by September 2027. If all options are exercised, work will continue through September 2033. Fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funding in the amount of $13,217,537 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the System for Award Management website, with two offers received. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-26-C-4313).

announcements.text: BCG Federal Corp., Bethesda, Maryland, was awarded a $100,000,000 firm-fixed-price contract (HT003826FE012), in support of the logical follow-on to the successful completion of the Design-to-Outcome Task Order Year 4 and Core Task Order Year Four. The contract provides Workforce 3.0, a fully managed end-to-end solution supporting the Program Executive Office, Defense Healthcare Management Systems (PEO DHMS) mid-office and back-office functions across the full PEO DHMS product portfolio. The Year Five Core Task Order continues execution of the Workforce 3.0 solution and implements the agreed upon Year Five Design-to-Outcome task order. The period of performance is Aug. 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds were obligated at the time of award. The place of performance is Arlington, Virginia. The Defense Health Agency, Defense Healthcare Management Systems Contracting Division, Arlington, Virginia, is the contracting activity. (Awarded July 30, 2026).
